Weekly vs. Biweekly vs. Monthly House Cleaning: Which Schedule Fits Your Home?

The right cleaning schedule depends on who lives in your home and how you live in it. Here's how to choose between weekly, biweekly and monthly visits.

Get My Instant QuoteCall (469) 210-8005

Published 2026-10-20 · Salt of the Earth Cleaning Co.

Once you've decided you'd like help keeping the house clean, the next question is how often. Weekly? Every other week? Once a month? There's no single right answer. The best schedule depends on who lives in your home, how much time you spend there and how much mess your days naturally create.

Here's a practical look at each option, who it suits and how to decide.

Start with a baseline clean

Whatever schedule you choose, recurring visits work best when the home starts from a clean baseline. If your home hasn't had a professional clean in a while, a deep cleaning first takes care of the built-up dust and grime on baseboards, fans and fixtures. After that, each recurring visit is about maintaining, not catching up.

Weekly house cleaning

Weekly cleaning means your home never gets far from clean. Kitchens and bathrooms get attention before build-up has a chance to form, floors stay clear of crumbs and hair, and you rarely spend your own evenings scrubbing.

Weekly is a great fit if:

  • You have a busy household with kids, several adults or frequent guests
  • You have pets that shed, especially more than one
  • Someone in the home has allergies and you want dust and dander kept low
  • You work from home, so the house sees heavy use every day
  • You simply want to stop thinking about cleaning altogether

Things to consider

Weekly is the most frequent option, so it's the biggest commitment. If your home stays fairly tidy between visits, you may find every other week covers your needs just as well.

Biweekly (every other week) house cleaning

Every-other-week cleaning is a popular middle ground. It's frequent enough that bathrooms and kitchens don't get away from you, but it gives you a little more breathing room between visits.

Biweekly is a great fit if:

  • You're a couple or a small family with a moderately busy schedule
  • You can handle light tidying, dishes and the occasional wipe-down between visits
  • You have a pet or two but stay on top of vacuuming
  • You want a consistently clean home without a weekly visit

Things to consider

In the second week, you'll likely notice floors and bathrooms more. A quick vacuum or a bathroom wipe-down mid-cycle keeps things feeling fresh until the next visit.

Monthly house cleaning

A monthly clean is a regular reset. It catches the dust, soap scum and floor grime that builds up over a few weeks, even when you keep up with daily tidying yourself.

Monthly is a great fit if:

  • You live alone or with one other person
  • You travel often or spend a lot of time away from home
  • You enjoy doing your own light cleaning but want help with the bigger jobs
  • You don't have pets, or have a pet that sheds very little

Things to consider

A month is long enough for kitchens and bathrooms to need real attention, so monthly visits often take longer than weekly or biweekly ones. You'll also do more of the in-between upkeep yourself.

How to choose: a few quick questions

Ask yourself:

  1. How many people and pets live here? More people and more fur usually mean more frequent visits.
  2. How much time do you spend at home? A home that's lived in all day gets dirty faster than one that's empty during work hours.
  3. What do you want to stop doing? If you never want to clean a bathroom again, go weekly. If you just want help with the deep stuff, monthly may be enough.
  4. How do you feel at the end of the second week? If the house feels like it's slipping by then, weekly is probably your answer. If it still feels fine, biweekly or monthly will work.

You aren't locked in, either. Plenty of households start biweekly and adjust once they see how their home feels between visits.

What about one-time cleans?

If you only need help before a party, after the holidays or before family visits, a one-time cleaning might be all you need. Moving? Our move-in / move-out cleaning is made for empty homes and walkthroughs.

Why recurring cleaning pays off

Recurring visits do more than keep your home tidy. When the same routine happens on a schedule, small jobs never turn into big ones, and you get your evenings and weekends back. We work hard to send the same trusted cleaner for each visit, so they learn your home and your preferences.
